reason: The passage narrates the oppression of the Israelites by the Egyptian elite and emphasizes divine selection of leaders (Moses and Aaron) based on God's calling rather than inherent superiority. Moses expresses self-doubt ('uncircumcised lips'), and Aaron's authority is granted by God's commission. The text shows the Egyptian magicians attempting to replicate divine miracles but failing—demonstrating that human power and status do not convey inherent excellence. The theological framework centers on God's covenant and redemptive action toward an oppressed people, not on any inherent superiority of the powerful. Pharaoh's hardened heart and resistance to divine will further undermine any notion that the elite possess inherent merit. The passage emphasizes vulnerability of regular people under tyranny and God's preference for the enslaved over their oppressors.
